diagram_math_checks.objects_and_maps: For a specified blowup step sigma_{i+1}:X_{i+1}->X_i, C_i is its specified regular center, C'_i=X'_i x_{X_i} C_i, and X'_{i+1}=X'_i x_{X_i} X_{i+1}. Horizontal left arrows are closed inclusions. Vertical maps have domains C'_i, X'_i, X'_{i+1} and codomains C_i, X_i, X_{i+1}, respectively; right horizontal arrows are sigma'_{i+1}:X'_{i+1}->X'_i and sigma_{i+1}:X_{i+1}->X_i.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Statement and proof 1.2, with def-multiple-test-blowup-and-controlled-transform fixing the exact step data.

diagram_math_checks.relations: Both small squares are Cartesian: the left one by the scheme-theoretic inverse-image center, the right one by associativity of the stated X-prime fibre products. In the right square phi_i sigma-prime_{i+1}=sigma_{i+1} phi_{i+1}; in the left square inclusion followed by phi_i equals projection to C_i followed by inclusion. No outer rectangle or isomorphism of centers with blowups is asserted.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Proof 1.2 and fibre-product projections. thm-blowup-base-change-flat, Statement and proof 1.1-3.1, supply the canonical blowup identification because phi_i is smooth, hence flat.

diagram_math_checks.relations: phi_{i+1} is smooth by base change of phi_i. The center is admissible by smooth order/SNC preservation. D-prime_{i+1}=phi_{i+1}^{-1}(D_{i+1})=(sigma-prime_{i+1})^{-1}(C-prime_i) follows from the commuting square and D_{i+1}=sigma_{i+1}^{-1}(C_i).
diagram_math_checks.justification: Proof 1.2, 2.1, 3.1; def-exceptional-divisor-blowup defines the exceptional subscheme as the scheme-theoretic inverse image; thm-smooth-morphisms-stable-base-change-composition and lem-order-and-snc-under-smooth-morphisms supply the indicated interfaces.

diagram_math_checks.relations: Empty inverse-image center gives an isomorphism and empty exceptional divisor. Nonempty Cartier centers can give isomorphic ambient blowup maps while retaining nonempty exceptional divisors. A whole-component center deletes that component. Inserted isomorphisms carry no center/new boundary. Exponent -mu and index i+1 in the controlled transform, and order after omitting empty boundary members, are retained exactly in original proof 3.1.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Proof 1.1, 1.2, 3.1 and the local definition def-multiple-test-blowup-and-controlled-transform explicitly distinguish these cases; lem-controlled-transform-is-well-defined supplies the actual ideal transform. No universal nonempty-exceptional claim is made for arbitrary centers.
